provider: Digital Research Alliance of Canada — 1 TB default object storage per project, up to 40 TB project / 100 TB nearline via Rapid Access Service

free_tier.stated: 'All Arbutus projects are allocated a default 1TB of object storage. If more is required, you can either request an additional 9TB available through our Rapid Access Service. More than 10TB must be requested and allocated under the annual Resource Allocation Competition.' The RAS policy adds: PIs 'can request additional storage resources in any General Purpose cluster without submitting a RAC application, up to a maximum of 40 TB of project storage and 100 TB of nearline storage', with the total across all clusters capped at those numbers.

egress.terms: Not metered in any doc; OpenStack Swift/S3 serve objects over HTTPS and buckets can be made public.

tooling: OpenStack Swift or S3 against the Arbutus object store; rclone/swift/s3cmd all work. 'We offer access to the OpenStack Object Store via two different protocols: Swift or Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3). ... object storage containers and objects created with Swift or S3 can be accessed using both protocols.'
chaining: 1 TB automatic + 9 TB RAS + up to 40 TB project storage per PI by email request. Multiple PIs/institutions each get their own; there is also a separate nearline (HPSS/tape) ceiling of 100 TB.

limits.value: application, up to a maximum of 40 TB of project storage and 100 TB of nearline storage', w

limits_note: per-object-cap: not documented for Arbutus. Retention: object storage is not backed up — 'management of a project's object storage containers is self-service. This includes operations such as backups because the object store itself is not backed up.' request-rate: not published. Gate: CCDB account (institutional), and storage above 10 TB requires an email to support@tech.alliancecan.ca from a PI.
reliability_note: Not backed up and self-managed; the docs are Anubis-protected (proof-of-work challenge) which also means scraping the current page fails and you must read the archived copy.
